https://mb.com.ph/2026/08/08/hungarian-e.text: Press Escape to quit searching Manila Bulletin Embassies & Foreign Affairs Hungarian envoy receives Order of Sikatuna Embassies & Foreign Affairs Hungarian envoy receives Order of Sikatuna By Manila Bulletin Published Aug 8, 2026 08:26 am President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. confers the Order of Sikatuna on outgoing Hungarian Ambassador Titanilla Tóth, accompanied by her spouse Arkadiusz Jan Tracz. (Photo: Philippine Communications Office) President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. conferred the Order of Sikatuna on outgoing Hungarian Ambassador to the Philippines Dr. Titanilla Tóth, recognizing her contributions to strengthening relations between the Philippines and Hungary as she concludes her diplomatic posting in Manila. Tóth received the honor during her farewell call on the President at Malacañan Palace on July 29. “It’s always a little bit sad to see you go. But thank you for everything that you have done,” Marcos told the ambassador, adding that she would have many reasons to return to the Philippines. The Order of Sikatuna is among the highest distinctions conferred by the Philippine government on foreign diplomats and officials who have contributed significantly to the country’s international relations. Established in 1953, the order takes its name from Datu Sikatuna of Bohol and the historic blood compact with Spanish explorer Miguel López de Legazpi in 1565. Hungarian Ambassador to the Philippines, Dr. Titanilla Tóth, paid a farewell courtesy visit to Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian. (Photo: Office of the Senate President) Tóth leaves Manila after a posting that saw Philippine-Hungarian cooperation expand across diplomacy, trade, education, agriculture, research, and cultural exchange. The Philippines and Hungary established diplomatic relations in 1973. In recent years, Hungary has also supported the early conclusion of negotiations for a Philippines-European Union Free Trade Agreement, which is expected to further expand opportunities for trade and investment. As part of her farewell engagements, Tóth met with Senate President Sherwin “Win” Gatchalian, with discussions touching on interparliamentary dialogue, educational cooperation, and people-to-people ties between the two countries. She also paid a farewell call on Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa P. Lazaro, where both sides looked back on developments in bilateral relations during her tenure. The Department of Foreign Affairs recognized the Hungarian Embassy’s work in promoting cultural diplomacy and educational exchanges, as well as cooperation in agriculture, research, trade, and other areas of mutual interest. Department of Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa P. Lazaro receives from Ambassador Dr. TitanillaTóth, copies of the books published by the Hungary Embassy, a collection of Hungarian poems translated into Filipino and regional languages. (Photo: Hungarian Embassy) Education has been an important component of Hungary’s engagement with the Philippines, complementing broader efforts to create stronger links between institutions and people in both countries. Tóth’s final round of meetings reflected the range of relationships cultivated during her posting—from the country’s highest political offices to institutions involved in education, culture, research, and commerce. Her departure closes one chapter in a diplomatic relationship now spanning more than five decades, with both Manila and Budapest looking to build on the areas of cooperation developed during her tenure. {{ articles_filter_1561_widget.title }} {{ item.title }} {{ static_articles_1562_widget.title }} {{ item.title }} {{ articles_filter_1563_widget.title }} {{ item.title }} {{ articles_filter_1564_widget.title }} {{ item.title }} {{ item.section_name }} | {{ item.sub_section_name }} {{ item.title }} {{ item.subtitle }} By {{ item.author_name }} Published {{ item.issue_date }} | Updated {{ item.last_edited }} Sponsored By At A Glance {{ line }} Read More Sign up by email to receive news. © 2025 Manila Bulletin The Nation's Leading Newspaper. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmz7.text: Image source, Reuters By Parul Gupta Published 9 October 2026 Three Saudi Arabian nationals have been killed in two attacks on the international airport in the capital, Riyadh, the country's civil aviation authority has said, after Yemen's Houthis said they had targeted the facility. The attacks also resulted in "injuries to a number of Saudi citizens and residents of various nationalities", the General Authority of Civil Aviation said in a statement on X. It added that the first attack on Thursday targeted the airport while the second had struck an aircraft belonging to state carrier Saudia. One of its pilots was among those killed, the airline said in a statement. Air traffic had returned to normal, the civil aviation authority said. Yemen's Houthi group said on Thursday it had attacked the airport with two ballistic missiles. The Iran-aligned group said it had also targeted an airport in Najran city near the Saudi border with Yemen, and Khamis Mushait air base further north. Saudi Arabia has not confirmed these attacks. The latest casualties follow the deaths of three people in Houthi attacks on two Saudi airports on 6 and 7 October. Two were killed and 28 wounded in an attack at Abha International Airport, the civil aviation body said on Wednesday. Another person was killed at King Khalid airport in Riyadh. The latest attacks come amid a marked escalation in renewed fighting between Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces and the Houthis, who control most of the country's north-west. The Houthi military spokesman said the previous two attacks on Saudi Arabia's airports were in "response to the Saudi aggression against our country" that saw "60 air strikes and missile attacks in the past 24 hours". The group says it is targeting Saudi Arabia over its support for government forces in Yemen's civil war. The conflict has worsened in recent weeks, after the Houthis seized strategically important stretches of the Red Sea coast in a rapid offensive. That included the port of Mokha on the Bab al-Mandab Strait, which is the narrowest point of the Red Sea and a chokepoint for global shipping. But Yemeni pro-government forces have since said they had "secured" the Bab al-Mandab Strait at the southern end of the Red Sea. A Saudi-led coalition was formed in 2015 after Arab countries joined forces to stop the Houthis taking over Yemen from the country's internationally recognised government. A temporary ceasefire was brokered in 2022 after years of air strikes and ground fighting led to the deaths of hundreds of thousands of people, triggering one of the world's worst humanitarian crises. But the informal ceasefire began to unravel in July. The Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea. They said they were retaliating against what they say is a years-long Saudi blockade and for an air strike on Sanaa airport. https://www.chesterstandard.co.uk/news/2.text: Court Crime Chester Ellesmere Port Criminals locked up in Chester during September 2026 Court Crime Chester Ellesmere Port By Matthew Dougherty Reporter Share 0 Comments 9 Skip to next photo 1 / 1 Show caption 1 / 1 Share 0 Comments This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. SEVERAL individuals were jailed last month following court cases in Chester. The Standard covers court hearings across magistrates and crown court – here is a list of criminals who were jailed during September 2026. Neil Tobijanski The 59-year-old was jailed for 26 months at a sentencing hearing at Chester Crown Court on September 2. He pleaded guilty to attempting to engage in sexual communication with a child, breaching a sexual harm prevention order (SHPO) breaching sex offender notification requirement. Read the full story here . (Image: Cheshire Police) Vincent Sulcana Sulcana was jailed for 27 months following a drunken assault in which he bit a man’s ear at a property in Knutsford. The 38-year-old pleaded guilty to inflicting grievous bodily harm without intent and was sentenced on September 21. Read the full story here . Vincent Sulcana. (Image: Cheshire Police.) Rory Need The 37-year-old received a six year and six month-sentence after he was found guilty of several sexual offences including possessing, making and distributing indecent images of children and engaging in sexual communication with a child. He was found guilty following a three-day trial and sentenced at Chester Crown Court on September 21. Read the full story here . Rory Need. (Image: Cheshire Police.) Aaron Bradley Bradley, 35 and of Summerton Road, Macclesfield, was sentenced to 45 months in prison at Chester Crown Court on September 18. He had pleaded guilty to being concerned in supply of class A drugs (cocaine) and possession of class B drugs (cannabis). Read the full story here . Aaron Bradley. (Image: Cheshire Police.) Damon Furmedge The 36-year-old, previously of Weaver Street, Winsford, was jailed for 14 years on September 10 following an eight-day trial at Chester Crown Court. Furmedge was convicted of rape, assault, and two counts of controlling and coercive behaviour in relation to a terrifying campaign of abuse. Read the full story here . (Image: Cheshire Police) Ethan Mason Mason was jailed for four years for child sexual offences following at a sentencing hearing at Chester Crown Court on September 9. The 22-year-old pleaded guilty to offences including making and distributing indecent images of children, engaging in sexual communication with a child and causing a child to engage in sexual activity. Read the full story here . (Image: Cheshire Police) Edgaras Dilys 31-year-old Dilys was jailed for more than six years following a hearing at Chester Crown Court on September 4. The Lithuanian national had been stopped on the M56 in Cheshire after he had thrown a 15kg bag of cocaine from a goods vehicle while driving through a border checkpoint when entering the UK. Read the full story here . (Image: Cheshire Police.) Matthew Gradwell Gradwell, 39, was jailed for six years and six months at Chester Crown Court on September 1 after admitting a series of offences, including causing serious injury by dangerous driving. The defendant, who had absconded from HMP Kirkham in December 2025, also pleaded guilty to three counts of burglary and theft, theft of motor vehicle, two counts of theft from a motor vehicle and driving while disqualified. Read the full story here . (Image: Cheshire Police) Court Crime Chester Ellesmere Port Share 0 Comments Get involved with the news Send your news & photos Loading... https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmx2.text: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Chancellor Friedrich Merz says Russian intelligence activity in Germany remains 'at a consistently high level' By Matt Spivey Published 4 hours ago Germany is the target of "intensive" espionage activity, Chancellor Friedrich Merz has said after a Ukrainian national was arrested on suspicion of spying for Russia. Officials said the suspect, named as Vadym Y., had allegedly collected military-related intelligence from Germany. Merz called the uncovering of the case a "success", but warned "let us not delude ourselves - the activities of Russian intelligence services in Germany remain at a consistently high level". Several people alleged to be acting on behalf of Russia and other foreign powers have been arrested in Germany this year. Germany has been one of the leading European suppliers of weapons to Ukraine since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022. The German Federal Prosecutor General's Office said on Thursday that Vadym Y., as he was identified under German privacy law, had been in contact with a Russian intelligence service through an intermediary since at least July 2025. It also said the Ukrainian man had collected information including "on the production of armoured vehicles, ammunition, and explosives". He is due to appear before an investigating judge on Friday. In January, a woman was arrested in Berlin suspected of gathering information for an intelligence officer at the Russian embassy. Other arrests this year included a Romanian woman and a Ukrainian man accused of spying on an individual supplying drones from Germany to Ukraine, according to the prosecutor's office. UK and Germany will face threats together, says Burnham in Berlin Published 8 October Trial of German steakhouse heiress that sparked a huge spy scandal Published 5 days ago Sabotage suspect held in Germany after spate of attacks on power grid Published 8 September And, the former German spy chief August Hanning was arrested on suspicion of espionage, treason and obtaining classified information for a foreign power earlier this month. Investigators have not disclosed which foreign powers were involved. Hanning headed the Federal Intelligence Service (BND) from 1998 to 2005 and has since been working as a private consultant. Police also arrested former BND employee Manfred D and accused him of passing Hanning about 2,000 classified documents in exchange for money. Speaking at the sidelines of a conference in Montenegro on Thursday, Merz said: "We will likely see more such cases in the coming months and years." Merz reaffirmed a series of defence and security partnerships with UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham earlier this month, including tackling hybrid attacks and hostile activity. The talks between the two leaders came after Germany accused Russia of launching a drone fitted with explosives at Leipzig/Halle Airport in September. Russian President Vladimir Putin accused Germany of planting evidence to blame Russia.
